Subject: Clarify retention defaults for API requests and outputs

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal and privacy teams have a few follow-ups about Redwood's default data retention behavior for the hosted API:

1) By default, how long does Redwood retain raw request/response payloads (we call these "requests") versus generated outputs (the "responses/outputs")? Does the default window differ between prompts (the input text) and model outputs?

2) Does retention vary by offering (hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC)? Specifically: are hosted API logs stored longer for model improvement than Dedicated seats?

3) Can customers opt out of retention on a per-request basis (header, SDK flag) or only account-level? Is there a documented deletion pathway we can point to?

4) For EU data residency requirements: if we set routing to EU, are request/response logs kept only in-region by default?

We need concise answers to include in our vendor risk assessment. If helpful, feel free to send a short PDF we can attach to our questionnaire.

Best,
Elena

Ben —

Below is a concise, customer-ready summary we can use. I included the operational deletion pathway and an opt-out note. If Legal wants tighter wording, flag it.

Policy summary (short):
- Default storage window (hosted API): Redwood stores request and response logs for 30 days by default. "Requests" include submitted prompts/inputs and request metadata; "responses/outputs" are the generated tokens and related metadata. Data retained within this window is used for debugging, metrics, and model improvement only when the customer has not opted out.
- Distinction: prompts are treated as part of the request object; outputs are treated as generated content. Both are subject to the same 30-day default retention window on the hosted service.
- Dedicated & Private: By default, Dedicated capacity does not send customer prompt/response content to Redwood's central model-improvement pipelines. Operational telemetry (latency, error traces) is retained for 90 days for SLO monitoring; content retention is configurable per contract and can be disabled. Private (VPC/on-prem) installations do not retain customer content in Redwood control plane by default; retention is controlled by the customer's infrastructure and agreement.
- Per-request opt-out: Customers may suppress persistent storage per request using the header X-Redwood-Store: false (SDK flag store=false available in v3 SDK). When set, requests are processed in-memory and not written to persistent logs. This does not affect ephemeral KV cache used for latency; KV cache may exist transiently in memory and is not written to long-term logs.
- Residency: When an account is configured for region: EU, all stored logs (for hosted API) are written to and retained in EU-hosted storage by default. Backups are tagged by region; for cross-region failover we have documented controls and would disclose them in the contract for customers with strict residency requirements.
- Deletion pathway: Customer-initiated deletion (portal or API) triggers removal from primary live stores within 72 hours. Full removal from incremental backup snapshots can take up to 90 days; we provide a deletion certificate when the process completes.
- Sensitive data & PII: We treat customer-supplied PII as customer data. For customers requiring that we do not use content for model improvement, we offer an opt-out that prevents training/aggregation pipelines from accessing data.

Action items / safe commits for sales:
1) We can provide Acme a 1-page PDF summarizing the bullets above (no raw logs included).
2) For EU residency claims, we can confirm logs remain in-region for accounts configured for EU by default; any cross-region replication is contractually disclosed.
3) If the customer needs per-request suppression, point them to the SDK flag (store=false) and we can include sample curl/SDK snippets.

Notes:
- The 30-day default is operationally necessary for incident triage and short-term debugging; it is not a training copy by default (training access requires explicit opt-in).
- For dedicated contracts we can add a provision to restrict/control central storage entirely.

I will prepare the short PDF and the SDK snippet. Neha — can you prepare the suggested customer wording and add a quick link to the docs? Rishi — anything to add on backup SLAs or deletion certificates?

Mina

Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — that language is good. Below is a one-paragraph summary and a docs blurb we can hand to Acme directly. I also opened a docs ticket (HS-1234567) to add the SDK flag example.

One-paragraph summary for vendor questionnaire (copy/paste):
"By default, Redwood retains request and response content for 30 days on our hosted API for debugging and metrics. Customers may opt out of persistent storage per request using the X-Redwood-Store: false header or the SDK flag (store=false). Dedicated and Private deployments do not route customer content to Redwood's model-improvement pipelines by default; retention for these deployments is contract-configurable. Accounts configured for EU residency store logs in-region by default; customer-initiated deletions purge live stores within 72 hours, with final removal from backups within 90 days. A deletion certificate can be provided on request."

Docs blurb (short):
- Default retention: 30 days for request/response content on hosted API.
- Opt-out: set X-Redwood-Store: false or use SDK store=false per request.
- Dedicated/Private: content storage is configurable; central model-improvement access is opt-in.
- Residency: region-specific storage for accounts configured with a region.

Neha
Senior Product Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
